text: Under the pale spring light of the Beren Ridge, the latest season at Tel Maridun has drawn attention for both its scale and its discipline. The excavation, begun in late March after two years of survey work, was led by Prof. Ansel Okafor of the Halden Institute, whose team opened three adjoining trenches near the eastern citadel wall. By midsummer, the group had logged 214 catalogued finds, including painted shardwork, bronze fittings, and a sealed storage pit believed to date to the site’s final occupation layer. Local records suggest Tel Maridun was first mapped in 1938, but this year’s campaign has been the most systematic yet. Okafor said the work was “less about spectacle than patience,” a remark that seemed to suit the place.
